edges.reason: msg.sender reaches the onlyOwner modifier of _authorizeUpgrade, so upgrade authorization depends purely on the caller identity
external msg.sender is the caller of upgradeTo, the entry point for replacing the implementation
mint requires hasRole(MINTER_ROLE, _msgSender()); privileged minting is keyed on msg.sender
pause requires hasRole(PAUSER_ROLE, _msgSender())
unpause requires hasRole(PAUSER_ROLE, _msgSender())
_setupRole grants DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, MINTER_ROLE and PAUSER_ROLE to _msgSender() during initialization
_authorizeUpgrade body is an empty onlyOwner modifier application, i.e. the authorization gate itself
the owner guard is exercised on the upgradeTo path
the owner guard is exercised on the upgradeToAndCall path
upgradeTo calls _authorizeUpgrade(newImplementation) before performing the upgrade
upgradeToAndCall calls _authorizeUpgrade(newImplementation) before performing the upgrade
upgradeTo reaches _upgradeToAndCallSecure which delegatecalls the new implementation during the upgrade
upgradeToAndCall delegatecalls the new implementation together with caller supplied data
_functionDelegateCall feeds the target address into the raw delegatecall, allowing arbitrary code execution before state is finalized
initialize calls __ERC20PresetMinterPauser_init which invokes the unchained initializer setting up roles
initialize configures the token metadata consumed by the overridden decimals()
the initializer grants privileged roles through _setupRole without any caller validation
mint forwards to the internal _mint, increasing totalSupply and recipient balance
the to parameter becomes the mint recipient in _mint
the amount parameter becomes the minted quantity in _mint
newImplementation is passed to _authorizeUpgrade, the only authorization hook of the upgrade mechanism
newImplementation flows into upgradeTo as the replacement implementation
newImplementation flows into upgradeToAndCall as the replacement implementation
the caller supplied data payload is delegatecalled by upgradeToAndCall during the upgrade
transferFrom reads _allowances[sender][_msgSender()] into the currentAllowance local variable
transferFrom computes currentAllowance - amount inside an unchecked block
the cached currentAllowance local is the operand of the unchecked subtraction
transferFrom triggers the _beforeTokenTransfer hook chain (pausable check) before balances are updated
hook implementations in the inheritance chain resolve the caller through _msgSender()
_mint writes the minted amount into the _balances state mapping
the unchecked subtraction result is written back into allowance/balance storage
decimals is a public view function reachable by any msg.sender

normalization_plan.reason: parameter name only feeds the ERC20 metadata initialization inside initialize and carries no independent security semantics
parameter symbol only feeds the ERC20 metadata initialization inside initialize and carries no independent security semantics
parameter newImplementation is validated through _authorizeUpgrade, so it should be normalized into that access-control function
parameter to is consumed directly by the _mint operation
parameter amount is consumed directly by the _mint operation
parameter data is delegatecalled by upgradeToAndCall, so it is absorbed by that function node
local variable currentAllowance exists only to feed the unchecked subtraction, so it merges into the unchecked arithmetic operation
